a multilevel interconnection network using wave-pipelining and multiplexing (WPM) can reduce the total power of a macrocell by almost a factor of 3, and can also reduce the total area by almost 20%.

the WPM interconnect network is a promising low power interconnect architecture that is able to reduce total power by almost 28%.

the design of low power interconnect networks for VLSI systems.
the development of a low power interconnect architecture that takes advantage of existing idleness to reduce power consumption.
the design of a low-power multilevel interconnection network.

the WPM interconnect network is an attractive alternative to traditional interconnect networks.
this paper presents a new interconnect architecture, WPM, that reduces power consumption by exploiting the inherent idleness of interconnect networks.

WPM can significantly reduce the power consumption of multilevel interconnection networks.

the power savings from WPM routing are not limited to the power savings from wire sharing, but also include the additional power savings from the redesigned interconnect network.
